question: What does F stand for in the FRBM Act, 2003 of the Indian economy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Bill (FRBM Bill) was introduced in India by the then Finance Minister of India, Mr.Yashwant Sinha in December 2000.
 
• The provisions provided in the initial versions of the bill were too drastic. After much discussion, a watered-down version of the bill was passed in 2003 to become the FRBM Act. The FRBM Rules came into force on July 5, 2004. 
 
• FRBM Act is all about maintaining a balance between Government revenue and government expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Objectives of the FRBM Act are:__

 
 
• To introduce transparent fiscal management systems in the country.
 
• To introduce a more equitable and manageable distribution of the country’s debts over the years.
 
• To aim for fiscal stability for India in the long run.
